name: SARMs-only cycle

lead: A SARMs-only cycle means taking one or more selective androgen receptor modulators (such as ostarine or LGD-4033) without steroids. Users frame it as gentler than steroids, with the appearance goal of faster muscle gain and leanness.
SARMs activate androgen receptors more in muscle and bone than in other tissues. Human trials of ostarine increased lean body mass, but no SARM is approved by the FDA or EMA.

paras: Forum users describe time-limited cycles run alongside training and diet, sometimes with testosterone checks, and discuss recovery afterwards. Specifics vary and are not covered here.

Reported effects include raised liver enzymes, lower HDL cholesterol and testosterone suppression; cardiovascular risk is unknown. SARMs are banned by WADA and are sold on a gray market where products are often mislabeled.

angle.text: Users report added muscle and a leaner physique during a cycle. The effect is on lean body mass; trial data come from clinical studies of ostarine.

lead: A SARMs-only cycle is a time-limited course of selective androgen receptor modulators without anabolic steroids. Looksmaxxing forum users describe it as a milder way to build muscle, lose fat and look more athletic.[1][2]

SARMs are drugs that act on the androgen receptor in tissues such as muscle and bone more than in others such as the prostate. The first nonsteroidal SARMs were developed in 1998. They are investigational; none is approved by the FDA or EMA as of 2023.[3] Ostarine is the most studied, with a phase III trial showing increased lean body mass but no significant functional improvement.[3]
Users on looksmax.org report muscle, strength and vascularity gains and ask about hair loss and post-cycle recovery.[2] Others argue that cycles end and gains revert.[4]

paras: Posters present SARMs-only plans as a way to avoid hair loss associated with some steroids, and report "huge muscle mass and strength gains".[2][4]
Skeptical posters call cycles a "cop out" because results revert after stopping.[4]

SARM side effects in clinical trials have been mild and infrequent, but include elevated liver enzymes, reduced HDL cholesterol, and suppression of gonadotropins and testosterone, varying by compound and dose; recreational use has been linked to liver injury case reports.[3]
Gray-market SARMs are often mislabeled and have led to prosecutions; the World Anti-Doping Agency banned them in 2008.[3]

Ostarine has been studied in about 25 trials with more than 1,700 participants; a phase III trial found increased lean body mass without significant functional improvement, and phase II urinary incontinence trials missed their endpoint.[3] No trial has tested a recreational SARMs-only cycle.

lore.intro: SARMs are discussed on looksmax.org as a milder alternative to steroids.[1][2][4]
